agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
summary: The Performance Incentive Grant Fund (PIGF/PJRA) is to reduce Maryland’s state and local incarcerated population through appropriate diversion, deflection, service provision and recidivism reduction resources.
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Government

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to reduce Maryland's incarcerated population. It supports evidence-based programs that improve reentry outcomes, reduce the impact of incarceration on communities, and lower recidivism. The fund also connects nonviolent offenders who have behavioral health needs with community treatment and support.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project grants. Funding comes from savings resulting from reforms under Maryland's Justice Reinvestment Act (JRA).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include community-based nonprofit organizations, local and state government agencies, and state and local courts.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can cover costs for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency projects releasing a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) in February and accepting applications in April.

summary: To reclaim and restore land and water resources adversely affected by past mining.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps reclaim coal mines that operated before 1977. It also restores streams affected by acid coal mine drainage. The program works to restore land and water resources damaged by past mining.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants to help restore land and water that past mining activities have affected.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves entities in Allegany and Garrett counties that are dealing with the effects of coal mining from before 1977.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds to reclaim coal mines that operated before 1977. You can also use funds to restore streams damaged by acid mine drainage.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in Allegany or Garrett counties.
requirements_list: Must address effects of coal mines that operated before 1977.

summary: The program provides mediation, counseling services, parent education, development of parenting plans and guidelines, visitation enforcement, and development guidelines for visitation and alternative custody arrangements.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program funds services for families. These services include mediation, counseling, and parent education. It also helps develop parenting plans, enforce visitation, and create guidelines for visitation and custody.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to organizations. These organizations then offer services like mediation, counseling, parent education, and help with creating parenting plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments and non-profit organizations that provide family services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support services for families, including: mediation, counseling, parent education, developing parenting plans, enforcing visitation, and creating visitation guidelines.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must respond to a Request for Proposals (RFP) through the eMMA system.

program_name: Administration-Sponsored Capital Grant Program for Mental Health, Addictions, and Developmental Disabilities Facilities
summary: Provide State grants on a match basis for construction, acquisition, renovation and equipping facilities that are used to serve clients with developmental disabilities, chronic mental illness and/or addiction problems.
application_due: Annually, due mid to late April

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides capital grants to help organizations acquire, design, construct, renovate, and equip facilities. These facilities must offer services for mental health, developmental disabilities, and substance abuse treatment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers capital grants to help pay for the costs of acquiring, designing, constructing, renovating, and equipping facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Organizations that provide services for mental health, developmental disabilities, or drug and alcohol abuse treatment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital costs, including: acquiring property, design work, construction, renovation, and purchasing equipment for facilities.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must download and complete the application and several required attachments from the program website.

summary: Multiple awards to incumbent licensed adult day care providers to provide a range of health and social services to elderly individuals with chronic health conditions to assist them to remain at home and in their community.
application_due: LHD are required to submit yearly budgets.  Day care centers are under contract 7/1/16 - 6/30/21.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to licensed medical day care centers. The centers use the funds to offer health, social, and support services to functionally disabled adults. This helps individuals stay in their homes and communities instead of moving to a nursing facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides contracts to licensed adult day care providers. The state sets the payment rates for these services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Day care centers are under contract 7/1/16 - 6/30/21.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed medical day care providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the delivery of health, social, and related support services in a structured group setting for functionally disabled adults.
requirements_list: Providers must be licensed under COMAR 10.12.04, Day Care for Elderly and Adults with a Medical Disability.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Health Departments submit yearly budgets. Day care centers operate under contract with the state.

summary: Advantage Maryland funds grants, loans and investments to support ED initiatives for business attraction, retention and infrastructure. Projects must be in a Priority Funding Area and eligible industry sectors. Awards are made on a competitive basis.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Government, Other
assistance_financial: Direct Loan, Direct Payment/Specified Use, Project Grant

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides conditional grants, loans, and investments to support economic development projects. It helps with business attraction, retention, infrastructure, brownfield redevelopment, and other local initiatives. Projects must be in a Priority Funding Area and in an eligible industry. The program awards funds on a competitive basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers five types of financing. These include funds for strategic and local economic development, direct assistance to local governments, revolving loan funds, and special purpose programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and political jurisdictions in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support business attraction and retention, infrastructure, brownfield redevelopment, arts and entertainment districts, daycare facilities, revolving loan funds, and local strategic planning.
requirements_list: Must have a County Resolution supporting the project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, contact the business development representative for your region to get more information.

summary: This program provides capital grants to assist in the preservation of buildings, sites, or communities of historical and cultural importance to the African American experience in Maryland.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Colleges, State University, State Government, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to help preserve buildings, sites, or communities that are historically and culturally important to the African American experience in Maryland. The Maryland Historical Trust and the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture jointly administer the program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers capital grants of up to $250,000 per project. Typically, the program has an annual budget of $5 million for grants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY26 African American Heritage Preservation Program round is now closed and is no longer accepting applications. The FY27 grant round is anticipated to open in March, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and individuals working to preserve sites related to African American heritage in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital projects, including: property acquisition; building rehabilitation and capital improvements; new construction; and predevelopment costs like studies, surveys, architectural plans, and engineering services.
requirements_list: The property or its proposed use must be associated with African American heritage.
The project must provide a strong public benefit to be competitive.
Work that is already underway or completed is not eligible for funding.
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties.
Applicants for cemetery projects must show clear property ownership.
The applicant must provide written permission from the property owner to undertake the project.
If the property is listed or eligible for the National Register, the owner must convey a term preservation easement to the Maryland Historical Trust.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The FY27 grant round is expected to open in March 2026. Typically, applications are available in early April and due by July 1. The agency announces decisions by December each year.

summary: Preserve productive agricultural land and woodland to insure future productive land is available to produce food and fiber.  The program purchases development rights easements on agricultural land.
eligibility: County Government, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional
assistance_financial: Direct Payment/Specified Use, Direct Payment/Unrestricted Use, Formula Grant, Project Grant, Tax Credit

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) protects farmland and woodland. The foundation buys agricultural preservation easements from landowners. These easements permanently stop development on the property. This program helps ensure land is available to produce food and fiber, stops random urban growth, protects open spaces and wildlife habitats, and improves the environmental quality of the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases agricultural preservation easements. This action permanently restricts development on prime farmland and woodland. The state has invested over $900 million in this program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners with productive farmland or woodland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program pays landowners to place a permanent conservation easement on their property. This easement restricts future development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program has preserved land in all 23 of Maryland's counties.
requirements_list: Land must be productive farmland or woodland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local program administrator or Foundation staff for more information. The website provides links to find their contact details.

program_name: Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts - Operating Support Grant
summary: Annual operating grants support activities, programs, and projects in A&E Districts throughout Maryland. Appointed management entities for designated A&E Districts may apply for MSAC operating support funds to support district priorities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides annual operating grants to support activities, programs, and projects in Maryland's Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts. Management entities appointed to run designated A&E Districts can apply for these funds to support district priorities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Arts Council, Department of Commerce
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides annual operating grants of $15,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Appointed management organizations for designated Arts & Entertainment Districts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds provide operating support for activities, programs, and projects that advance the priorities of a designated Arts & Entertainment District.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is for the appointed management entities of state-designated Arts & Entertainment (A&E) Districts.
requirements_list: Must be the appointed management entity of a designated A&E District in Maryland.
Must be a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization.
Must have a letter of agreement with the county or municipality that holds the A&E District designation.
Must have a current contract or memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a county or municipality to manage the designated A&E District.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The management entity for an A&E District submits an application annually. In the fifth year after designation, the entity submits a detailed 'On-Year' application. In all other years, it submits a shorter 'Off-Year' application. The A&E Districts Advisory Committee reviews on-year applications, while MSAC staff reviews off-year ones. The MSAC Council and the Secretary of Commerce give final approval for all funding.

summary: The Arts Capital grant program provides organizations with direct access to state capital funding for projects that enhance or create complete, usable, and accessible arts facilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives arts organizations state funds for capital projects. The projects should improve or create complete and accessible arts facilities. Funds can support expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants from $50,000 to $500,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for Maryland-based 501(c)3 nonprofit arts organizations that own or lease a physical property in the state.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for capital projects. This includes expanding, producing, renovating, or making major repairs to a facility or its infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland and the project facility must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-based 501(c)3 nonprofit organization.
Must operate a physical property in Maryland that is either leased or owned.
Must have an annual operating budget of less than $3,000,000.
Must either participate in MSAC’s Grants for Organizations or County Arts Development programs, or be open to the public and provide arts-based cultural education or experiences.
Must provide proof of property ownership or a lease agreement with at least five years remaining at the time of application.
Previous grantees must have completed their prior projects and submitted final reports before re-applying.
Cannot have received $500,000 in Arts Capital funds within a five-year period.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First-time applicants should contact program staff before applying. All organizations apply through the SmartSimple online system. A statewide panel reviews all applications. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) will notify all applicants of their decision electronically.

summary: Arts in Education grants provide funds to Teaching Artists on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster to support educational engagements at Maryland-based nonprofit organizations, schools, and other government entities.
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to support teaching artists from the Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) Roster. The funds help these artists run arts education programs in Maryland's schools and communities to encourage lifelong learning in the arts.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants up to a maximum of $6,000. The final amount depends on the applicant's request.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis between July 2025 and January 2026. The application deadlines are: September 5, 2025, November 5, 2025, January 5, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for teaching artists on the Maryland State Arts Council's (MSAC) Teaching Artist Roster who collaborate with Maryland schools, nonprofit organizations, or government entities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support teaching artists to implement arts education programs. These programs can take place in Maryland schools, libraries, community centers, detention centers, and other nonprofit or government locations.
requirements_list: The teaching artist must be on the MSAC Teaching Artist Roster.
The collaborating school or community site must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit, a unit of government, or a college/university in Maryland.
The collaborating site must have operated for at least one full fiscal year with ongoing arts activities.
A school or community site may participate in up to two grants per fiscal year.
Individual lead artists may receive a maximum of $21,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
Teaching artist organizations may receive a maximum of $84,000 in grant awards for FY 2026.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the teaching artist and the school or organization agree to collaborate on services, timelines, and fees. Second, the school or organization identifies a coordinator for the project. Third, the teaching artist or their affiliated organization starts and submits the application online using SmartSimple. A panel then reviews applications, and the applicant receives a notification the following month.

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative program aims to demonstrate how strategic investment in local housing and businesses can lead to healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life. The program attempts to focus on areas where modest investment and a coordinated strategy will have an appreciable neighborhood revitalization impact.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) invests in local housing and businesses. This investment helps create healthy, sustainable communities. It also aims to grow the tax base and improve the quality of life. The program focuses on areas where a coordinated strategy can make a big impact.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds:
Funds can support various activities, including:
- Down payment assistance for homebuyers.
- Acquiring or fixing vacant or blighted properties.
- Improving existing homes and businesses.
- Making properties more energy efficient.
- Developing mixed-use projects with housing, retail, and office space.
- Creating or improving community open spaces and public infrastructure.
- Supporting workforce and employment programs.
- Strategic demolition.
- Covering operating costs for community projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City and the inner beltway areas of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
requirements_list: Applicants must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan. If a plan is not yet approved, it must be submitted with the application.
Applying with partner organizations, like Community Development Financial Institutions, is strongly recommended.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To get more information and apply, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage. If your organization does not have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan, you must submit one with your project application.

program_name: Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (formerly Project CORE)
agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: The Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative provides public and nonprofit partners in Baltimore City grant funding to address vacant properties through acquisition, stabilization, demolition and other pre-development activities, clearing the way for new green space or affordable housing and mixed-use developments.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides capital to community development organizations in Baltimore City. The funds help them redevelop properties that have vacant building notices. Organizations can use the money to acquire, stabilize, renovate, or demolish these properties to improve neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants and loans to finance projects that address vacant properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit community development organizations and local governments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for several activities. These include acquiring, stabilizing, and renovating vacant buildings. You can also use funds to buy and combine vacant lots for new housing or community green space. Money is also available for urgent demolition and other pre-development work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City. The program gives special consideration to projects within the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geography.
requirements_list: Funded community development organizations may need to provide a government resolution, a corporate board resolution, and proof of charitable registration.

summary: BIITC provides refundable income tax credits to eligible investors in Qualified Maryland Biotechnology Companies (QMBC) equal to 33% or 50% of an eligible investment in a QMBC, up to $250,000 or $500,000 in tax credits.
application_due: Two different forms are due in August and September. See website for dates.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a refundable income tax credit to investors in qualified Maryland biotechnology companies (QMBCs). The credit is typically 33% of the investment, up to $250,000. The credit increases to 50%, up to $500,000, for investments in companies located in specific counties. Enhanced credits are also available for investments in companies within Opportunity Zones and RISE Zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Investors receive a refundable income tax credit. The standard credit is 33% of the investment, up to $250,000. A higher 50% credit, up to $500,000, is available for investments in companies in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset counties. Enhanced credits of up to 75%, with a maximum of $750,000, are also available for investments in companies within designated Opportunity Zones or RISE Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals and business entities that invest in qualified Maryland biotechnology companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The biotechnology company receiving the investment must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland. Enhanced tax credits are available for investments in companies located in Allegany, Dorchester, Garrett, or Somerset counties, or in designated Opportunity Zones or RISE Zones.
requirements_list: Investor must invest at least $25,000.
Investor must be required to file an income tax return in a non-tax haven jurisdiction.
Biotechnology company must have its headquarters and base of operations in Maryland.
Biotechnology company must have fewer than 50 full-time employees.
Biotechnology company must be in active business for 12 years or less.
Total tax credits for all investors in a single company cannot exceed $7,000,000.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the biotechnology company submits a QMBC application online. Second, the investor submits an investor application online by the deadline. Third, the investor uses an assigned username and reference number to register for an online queue which determines funding priority. Commerce then reviews applications and issues an initial approval. After receiving approval, the investor makes the investment and provides proof to Commerce. Finally, Commerce issues a final tax credit certificate.

summary: The Brownfields Revitalization Incentive Program promotes economic development and environmental improvement, especially in distressed urban areas, by identifying and redeploying underutilized properties. A property tax abatement is available for qualifying properties in jurisdictions that have elected to participate in the program.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps improve the environment and economy, especially in distressed urban areas. It encourages the cleanup and reuse of underutilized properties. The program offers a property tax credit to eligible properties in participating local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: For five years after a site cleanup, a property can get a real property tax credit. The credit is between 50% and 70% of the new property tax amount caused by the increase in the property's value. If the property is in an Enterprise Zone, the tax credit can last for up to 10 years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Property owners or operators who are not responsible for the contamination of a qualifying brownfield site.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides a tax credit against property taxes for the cleanup and redevelopment of eligible brownfield sites.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The property must be located in a participating jurisdiction. This includes specific counties and municipalities that have chosen to offer the tax credit.
requirements_list: The site must be in a jurisdiction that participates in the program.
The owner or operator must be an 'inculpable person,' meaning they are not responsible for the contamination.
The property must be accepted into the Maryland Department of the Environment’s (MDE) Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP).
MDE must issue a closure document, such as a Certificate of Completion or a No Further Requirements Determination.
The jurisdiction must issue a building permit for the project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, request a qualification letter from the Department of Commerce. To do this, submit a completed General Application, the BRIP addendum, and copies of letters from the Maryland Department of Environment (MDE). These MDE letters must show the property's acceptance into the Voluntary Cleanup Program, your 'inculpable person' status, and a final closure document. You must also provide a copy of the building permit. After Commerce issues the qualification letter, you can take it to your local jurisdiction to apply for the tax credit.

program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
summary: The Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund provides grants for innovative and transformative infrastructure projects that accelerate the growth of eligible strategic industry sectors.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University

structured_extraction.program_name: Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives grants for large infrastructure projects. These projects help grow important technology industries in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers matching grants up to $2 million. For grants up to $1 million, you must provide matching funds equal to at least 200% of the grant amount. For grants over $1 million, you must provide matching funds equal to at least 400% of the grant amount.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are not being accepted for the remainder of FY2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for private companies, non-profit organizations, local governments, and colleges or universities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds to acquire, build, renovate, install, improve, or equip an eligible project. Examples include wet laboratories, cyber ranges, and specialized training spaces. You cannot use grant funds for indirect costs like salaries or management fees.
requirements_list: Applicants must provide matching funds. The required match is 200% for grants up to $1 million and 400% for grants between $1 million and $2 million.
Funds from other State grant programs do not count toward the matching requirement.
Applicants must show they can pay for their share of the project costs.
A single organization cannot receive more than $2 million in one fiscal year.
Colleges and universities cannot receive more than 50% of the total funds available in a fiscal year.
Projects from colleges and universities must collaborate with private industry or show a significant potential for economic impact.
Grant funds must be spent within two years of the agreement date.
The project must be fully operational within two years of the agreement date.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application has two steps. First, applicants submit an initial project summary. A review committee then invites a limited number of applicants to submit a more detailed second application.

summary: Tax credit provides an incentive for qualified Maryland companies to purchase cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives a tax credit to Maryland companies that buy cybersecurity products and services from qualified Maryland sellers. The credit helps small businesses protect their information and supports the state's cybersecurity industry.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Companies can receive a tax credit for 50% of the cost of cybersecurity products and services. The maximum credit is $50,000 per year, which covers up to $100,000 in purchases. The program has a total of $4 million available each year. Of this, $3 million is for technology purchases and $1 million is for service purchases.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses with fewer than 50 employees that are required to file a state income tax return.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase eligible cybersecurity technologies and services from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller. Technologies must be proprietary products designed to protect information systems and data. Services must align with the most recent National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to businesses operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have fewer than 50 employees in Maryland
Must be required to file a Maryland income tax return
Purchase must be from a Qualified Maryland Cybersecurity Seller
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Before you apply, you must contact Cindy Zeng at cindy.zeng@maryland.gov, as some sellers have reached their funding cap for the current tax year. After confirming eligibility, submit an application online. The Department of Commerce will not accept applications in other formats. If approved, you will receive a Certificate of Approval. You must attach this certificate to your Maryland income tax return.

program_name: Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Bryne SCIP/BSCI)
agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
summary: Authorized by the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (BSCA) of 2022 (Pub. L. No. 117-159, 136 Stat. 1313, 1339), the Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP) provides states with funding to implement firearm violence reduction strategies at the intersections of behavioral health and domestic violence including but not limited to state crisis intervention court proceedings and extreme risk protection orders (ERPO).
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State Government, Other

structured_extraction.program_name: Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program (Byrne SCIP/BSCI)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Byrne State Crisis Intervention Program gives states money to reduce gun violence. It focuses on issues where behavioral health and domestic violence meet. The program supports state crisis intervention courts and extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs).
structured_extraction.agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides formula-based grant funding to states. The funds support crisis intervention programs that aim to reduce firearm violence.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for community-based non-profits, domestic violence programs, victim service providers, higher education institutions, law enforcement agencies, religious organizations, courts, and state government agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support state crisis intervention programs. This includes extreme risk protection order (ERPO) programs, mental health courts, drug courts, and veteran treatment courts. Money can also be used for training, public awareness campaigns, behavioral health services for at-risk individuals, and helping law enforcement safely handle relinquished guns.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA). Applicants should follow the instructions in the NOFA to apply.

summary: The Cannabis Business Assistance Fund provides grants and loans for small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry. The Fund also provides grants to HBCUs for cannabis-related programs, and to business development organizations to train and assist licensed small businesses.
eligibility: For-Profit, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce runs the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund. This fund gives grants and loans to small businesses entering the adult-use cannabis industry, especially those owned by minorities and women. The fund also offers grants to Historically Black Colleges and Universities for cannabis programs and to groups that train new cannabis entrepreneurs. A current grant opportunity is available for Social Equity Applicants with a conditional license.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants and loans. A specific grant for Social Equity licensees offers funding based on license type. A standard dispensary can get up to $131,250, a processor up to $183,750, and a grower up to $525,000. Businesses with micro-licenses receive smaller amounts. The grant is paid in four parts as the business meets specific goals.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application portal opened on June 3, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program helps small businesses entering the adult cannabis market, with a focus on minority-owned and women-owned companies. It also supports Historically Black Colleges and Universities and business organizations that train cannabis entrepreneurs. Current funding is for Social Equity Applicants who have a conditional cannabis license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can help pay for license applications. Businesses can also use the money for operating costs and capital expenses. The funds can also pay for targeted training to support participation in the adult-use cannabis industry.
requirements_list: Must meet the minimum Adequate Capital Requirement set by the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA).
Must be an existing business in Good Standing with the State of Maryland.
Must be a small business with 0-50 employees per license.
The business must hold a Maryland Social Equity Cannabis Business Conditional License.
The business must be at least 51% owned by individuals with a personal net worth not exceeding $1.7 million.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, register for access to the application portal on the Department of Commerce website. It is best to register before you request your first payment. You will need several documents, including your lottery number, conditional license letter, personal net worth information for owners, a W-9 form, and proof that your business is in Good Standing with Maryland.

program_name: Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH)
summary: Provides culturally-informed and language-accessible public health services and health education to newly-arrived refugees, asylees, and other humanitarian immigrants.

structured_extraction.program_name: Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health (CGMIH)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Center for Global Migration and Immigrant Health partners with health centers, providers, and community groups. The center helps ensure newly arrived humanitarian immigrants get health assessments, follow-up care, and education. The program also helps migrant and seasonal farm workers access healthcare, including immunizations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides comprehensive health assessments, follow-up care, care coordination, referrals, and health education for humanitarian immigrants. It also offers technical assistance, resources, and training to healthcare and community associations that work with these populations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves newly arrived humanitarian immigrants, including refugees and asylees, as well as migrant, seasonal, and agricultural workers. It also supports health centers, health providers, and community organizations that work with these groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This program provides services. Key activities include: Identifying and addressing public health conditions through health assessments and treatment. Connecting immigrants to culturally-informed healthcare. Providing health education about the U.S. healthcare system. Offering technical assistance and training to partner organizations. Developing and sharing health education materials.

program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund (Trust Fund)
summary: The Trust Fund funds the most cost-effective, efficient nonpoint source nutrient and sediment reduction project proposals in geographic targeted areas of the state.
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_name: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This fund supports cost-effective projects that control pollution from runoff. The program aims to speed up the restoration of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding for cost-effective projects that control pollution from non-point sources to improve water quality.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for local and state government entities, non-profit organizations, and state colleges and universities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that control non-point source pollution. This includes restoring streams and floodplains, enhancing forest buffers near rivers, improving wetland ecosystems, and managing stormwater.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide but gives priority to projects in specific targeted areas shown on a map to maximize pollution reduction.
requirements_list: Projects must be cost-effective and focus on controlling non-point source pollution.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the Grants Gateway portal. A link is available on the program website.

summary: Supports the goals and strategies developed under the 2014 Chesapeake Watershed Agreement.  Implementation tasks support the Chesapeake Bay Program's collective commitment to restoring and protecting the Bay through 10 goals and 31 outcomes.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps Maryland achieve the goals of the 2014 Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement. The program funds projects that support the agreement's management strategies. It focuses on improving water quality by reducing nutrient and sediment pollution. The funds also support other goals like sustainable fisheries, vital habitats, and climate resiliency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funding to partners. Applicants must provide a 1:1 non-federal match for the funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include state agencies, the University of Maryland system, local governments, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that help restore and protect the Chesapeake Bay. This includes efforts to reduce water pollution, improve fisheries and habitats, address toxic contaminants, and enhance climate resiliency.
requirements_list: Requires a 1:1 non-federal match

agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
summary: Child Advocacy Centers stress coordination of investigative and intervention services by bringing together professionals and agencies as a multi-disciplinary team to create a child-focused approach to child abuse cases.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports Child Advocacy Centers, which coordinate investigation and intervention services for child abuse cases. The centers bring together professionals from different agencies into a multi-disciplinary team. This child-focused approach helps prevent further trauma to children during the legal process.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state provides annual funding for this program through grants. These funds must add to, not replace, money the programs get from other sources.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Yvette Williams (Grant Monitor), Jennifer Krabill (Fund Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants are Designated Child Advocacy Centers and the Maryland Children's Alliance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel.
requirements_list: Applicants must be a Designated Child Advocacy Center or the Maryland Children's Alliance.
Funding must supplement, not supplant, existing funds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), typically in April. Applicants then apply, usually in May, through the online Grant Management System (GMS).

program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
summary: Funds are used to offset meal and supplement costs to public, private nonprofit or proprietary centers licensed to provide non-residential childcare services for daycare homes, eligible centers and non-residential eligible adult daycare centers.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps licensed daycare providers pay for nutritious meals and snacks for children, older adults, and people with disabilities in their care.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides money to help cover the costs of meals and snacks.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for licensed daycare homes and non-residential adult daycare centers, including public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help pay for the cost of nutritious meals and snacks for participants.
requirements_list: Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: The NourishMD Grant Program expands access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible retailers.

structured_extraction.featured_description: Grants of up to $150,000 to support capital-related needs for grocery stores and markets in areas with limited healthy food access.
structured_extraction.program_description: The NourishMD Grant Program expands access to fresh foods in food-insecure communities. It provides grants to eligible food retailers to support operations and improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards grants between $25,000 and $150,000. A total of up to $2 million is available for funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include grocery stores, corner stores, co-ops, farm stands, farmers' markets, delivery retailers, and small food-focused stores.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recipients use funds for equipment like refrigeration and shelving, facility upgrades, inventory expansion capital, working capital, and SNAP/EBT technology.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility:
Businesses must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher.

Note: Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible for the NourishMD grant program.

However, if you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email us at compass@maryland.gov. We aim to make Compass as comprehensive as possible and would like your help to do so!
requirements_list: Must operate at least 5 days per week, year-round (farmers markets and on-farm markets are exempt).
Must currently offer or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods.
Must dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items.
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality.
A $250 processing fee is sourced from the award amount.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a complete application through the DHCD portal between January 20 and February 20. The agency reviews applications in February and March and finalizes recommendations in April. Award notifications occur in May, followed by disbursements in June.

program_name: Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund
summary: The Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund provides no-interest loans for capital expenses to child care providers who participate in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program.

structured_extraction.featured_description: No-interest loans for capital expenses to child care providers who participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Commerce manages this fund. It offers no-interest loans to child care providers for capital expenses. To qualify, providers must participate in the State Department of Education's Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides no-interest loans. There are no application fees. Borrowers must repay the loan within five years. There are no penalties for paying the loan back early.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland child care providers who are licensed and participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loans pay for capital expenses like buying a building, expanding space, renovating, or new construction. Funds cannot pay for operations, working capital, or refinancing old debt.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide. It gives priority to providers in rural areas, underserved communities, and areas that lack enough child care slots.
requirements_list: Must have a valid child care license from the Maryland State Department of Education.
Must participate in the Child Care Scholarship Program.
Must repay the loan within five years.
Must provide collateral to secure the loan.
Must not use funds for refinancing existing debt or general operations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must apply through the online portal by January 30, 2026. The application requires details on ownership, a valid license, and proof of scholarship participation. Applicants must also submit financial projections, tax returns, and collateral details.

agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
summary: The Children's Justice Act provides grants to improve the investigation, prosecution and judicial handling of cases of child abuse and neglect, particularly child sexual abuse and exploitation.
eligibility: County Government, Non-Profit, State Government, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to states to improve the way they handle child abuse and neglect cases. It focuses on the investigation, prosecution, and judicial process for these cases, especially those involving child sexual abuse. The main goal is to limit additional trauma to child victims.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants to help improve how the state manages child abuse and neglect cases.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Yvette Williams (Grant Monitor), Jennifer Krabill (Fund Manager)
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for local and state government agencies, law enforcement, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can pay for contractual services, equipment, operating expenses, personnel, and travel.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), typically in May. The projected application period is in July.

summary: Provide regulatory oversight of contaminated properties not participating in the Voluntary Cleanup Program through the Technical Review Service and enforcement through Controlled Hazardous Substances regulations.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides regulatory oversight for contaminated properties not in the Voluntary Cleanup Program. It uses a Technical Review Service and enforces Controlled Hazardous Substances regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers project grants. It also provides regulatory services and technical assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves government bodies, for-profit companies, individuals, non-profits, and state colleges or universities responsible for contaminated properties not enrolled in the Voluntary Cleanup Program.
requirements_list: Applicant must be responsible for a contaminated property not participating in the Voluntary Cleanup Program.

program_name: Commercial, Industrial, and Agricultural Grant Program (CI&A)
summary: The Commercial, Industrial, and Agricultural Grant Program will offer competitive grants to commercial, industrial, agricultural, and non-profit enterprises undertaking deep retrofits that significantly reduce facility energy consumption.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers competitive grants to Maryland businesses and non-profits. The grants help pay for energy-saving improvements in commercial, industrial, and data center facilities. The program supports both new construction projects and upgrades to existing buildings.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides competitive grants from a total budget of up to $8.4 million. For facilities where over 50% of clients are from low-income populations, grants may cover 100% of project costs. For all other projects, grants cover less than 100% of costs. Applicants may also apply for a separate loan to finance the remaining project balance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for owners of commercial facilities, industrial facilities, data centers, and non-profits located in Maryland. Eligible businesses include corporations, LLPs, LLCs, and GPs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are for energy efficiency improvements in new or existing buildings. Projects must result in energy performance that is better than current codes or standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must own or operate facilities located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must result in energy performance that exceeds current codes or standards.
Multifamily residential buildings must contain five or more units.
To qualify for 100% project cost coverage, the facility must demonstrate that over 50% of its clientele are from low-income populations.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This is a competitive grant program. Applicants must submit a complete proposal by the deadline. The Maryland Energy Administration scores applications based on the quality of documentation and the project's environmental benefits. The agency awards grants in rank order until the program funds are fully allocated.

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: Community Investment Tax Credits support 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits for use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services.  See also www.GiveMaryland.org

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps nonprofit organizations attract donations from individuals and businesses. It gives state tax credits to donors who contribute to approved local projects and services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individuals and businesses who donate $500 or more to a qualified project can earn a state tax credit. The credit equals 50% of the value of their contribution, which can be money, goods, or real estate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support capital and operating projects. This includes activities like education and youth services, housing and community development, job training, neighborhood enhancement, arts and culture, economic development, and services for at-risk groups.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: Applicants must be an IRS-designated 501(c)(3) organization.
Donations must be $500 or more to qualify for tax credits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, you must register through the Application Portal. Select 'New User?' and fill out the registration form. It may take up to 72 hours for your registration to be approved.

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: The Community Legacy program provides local governments and community development organizations with funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities through activities such as business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership and commercial revitalization.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Legacy program gives money to local governments and community development groups. The funding supports projects that make communities stronger. These projects include keeping and attracting businesses, helping people own homes, and revitalizing business districts.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for local governments and non-profit community development organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects like: mixed-use residential, commercial, and open space development; business support, including retention, expansion, and attraction; streetscape improvements; programs to increase homeownership and home repairs; building facade improvements for homes and businesses; property acquisition, land banking, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a designated Sustainable Community. Alternatively, projects in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, or Wicomico counties can be located in an Opportunity Zone.
requirements_list: Project must help achieve the local government’s Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, applicants should visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage for more information and instructions.

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: Through annual awards to designated Community Action Agencies, CSBG funds alleviate the causes and conditions of poverty in Maryland by addressing the needs of low-income individuals in the areas of employment, education, better use of available income, housing, nutrition, emergency services and/or health.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to seventeen Community Action Agencies across Maryland. These agencies use the money to offer services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies. The state uses the other 5% for discretionary funding to support activities that fight poverty.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units that serve low-income individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support direct services for low-income individuals to help them become self-sufficient. This can include programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Funds can also support training, technical assistance, and community revitalization projects.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period for fiscal year 2025 has closed. You should check the program's webpage for information about future application opportunities.

summary: Provides funding to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations to offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) enabling clean energy to be offered to Low-to-Moderate Income (LMI), overburdened, and underserved communities at lower cost.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funds to Community Solar Subscriber Organizations. The money helps lower the cost of Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), which are contracts for buying electricity. This allows organizations to offer clean energy to low-income households at a reduced price.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program has an anticipated budget of approximately $17 million. This funding comes from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Solar Subscriber Organizations are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds offset costs associated with Power Purchase Agreements. This helps provide clean energy to low-income households at a lower cost.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This is a statewide competitive program.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must review the Funding Opportunity Announcement and use the provided application worksheet and checklists to apply.

summary: Commuter Choice promotes alternatives to driving alone such as public transportation, ridesharing, walking, biking, teleworking, alternative work schedules, Maryland Commuter Tax Credit, and Guaranteed Ride Home.
application_due: Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually

structured_extraction.program_description: The Commuter Choice Maryland program helps employers and commuters reduce traffic congestion. It provides resources to make commuting easier, safer, cheaper, and greener.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers state and federal tax benefits to Maryland employers and commuters. It also provides a mobile app called CommuterCash. Users can log commute trips to earn points and redeem them for cash, gift cards, or transportation credits.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration for the Maryland Commuter Tax Credit should be completed annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program serves Maryland employers and commuters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides tax benefits and cash rewards to encourage alternatives to driving alone, such as using public transportation, carpooling, biking, or teleworking.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Employers and commuters can find more information on the program's website. To earn cash rewards, users download the CommuterCash mobile app and log their trips. Employers must register annually to receive the tax credit.

program_name: Conservation Easement Program - Conservation Property Tax Credit
summary: Program encourages donation of conservation easements and gives participating landowners, a 15-year property tax credit on unimproved land under easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust.

structured_extraction.program_name: Conservation Easement Program - Conservation Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a 15-year property tax credit to landowners who donate a conservation easement to the Maryland Environmental Trust. The credit applies to unimproved land covered by the easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a full property tax credit for 15 years on unimproved land under a donated conservation easement. The credit does not apply to residential buildings or at least one acre of land surrounding them. After 15 years, the property is assessed at the highest agricultural rate, which may result in lower future taxes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications may be filed for the fiscal tax year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland landowners
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: This program is available to landowners throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: The easement must be donated to the Maryland Environmental Trust or the Department of Natural Resources.
The easement must be perpetual.
The Board of Public Works must approve the easement.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, download the Conservation Property Tax Credit Application form. Then, file the completed application with your county's Office of the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation for the fiscal tax year. You must attach a copy of the recorded Deed of Conservation Easement and the Board of Public Works approval letter to your application.

summary: County Arts Development Grants provide grants and technical assistance to county arts councils and Baltimore City to better serve artists, organizations, and audiences and to encourage local decision-making, arts activity, and funding for the arts.

structured_extraction.program_description: The County Arts Development (CAD) grant program supports county arts agencies in Maryland. The program helps these agencies connect with artists, arts organizations, and local communities. It also encourages local arts activities and provides fair funding for the arts at the county level.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides formula-based grants to support county arts agencies. It also offers technical assistance to help applicants with their plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for official county arts agencies, which can be local government agencies or designated nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the operations of county arts agencies. This includes their own grant-making activities and other programs that serve local artists, arts organizations, and audiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is open to the officially designated arts agency or council for each of Maryland's 23 counties and Baltimore City.
requirements_list: Must be a local agency or nonprofit designated by the jurisdiction's government as the official arts agency or council.
Submit an application annually, which will be either a detailed three-year plan ('On-Year') or a shorter update ('Off-Year').
Grantees must submit interim and annual final reports detailing the use of funds.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Designated county arts agencies submit one of two types of applications each year. Every three years, an agency submits an 'On-Year' application with a detailed three-year plan. MSAC staff and a review panel review a draft and provide feedback. The agency revises the plan and submits it for final Council approval. In the two years between, the agency submits a simpler 'Off-Year' application. This application notes any changes to the three-year plan and includes required financial reports.

program_name: Creativity Grant for General Operating Support
summary: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support strengthen the vitality and sustainability of small organizations to maintain a strong and stable arts infrastructure in Maryland. This option is available to organizations only.
application_due: Rolling. MSAC is currently accepting applications for the FY2026 application cycle.

structured_extraction.program_name: Creativity Grants for General Operating Support
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to support the general operations of small arts organizations in Maryland. The grants help maintain a strong and stable arts community in the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Arts Council, Department of Commerce
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants of up to $4,000 for general operating support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants are small arts organizations in Maryland, including 501(c)3 nonprofits, local government units, and colleges or universities. Independent artists are not eligible for this specific grant.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support an organization's overall operations for an entire season or fiscal year.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The organization must be incorporated in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college/university.
Must produce or present arts programs, services, or projects that are available to the public.
Cannot be a current participant in the Grants for Organizations (GFO), County Arts Development (CAD), or Arts & Entertainment District (A&E) programs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit their application through the SmartSimple online portal. A panel reviews applications monthly. The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC) notifies applicants of their status. If approved, the grantee receives a grant agreement to process payment, which can take up to 90 days.

summary: Creativity Grant for Projects strengthen the vitality and sustainability of artists and small organizations and provide opportunities to serve the growing needs of relevant arts projects and collaborations within Maryland communities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant helps artists and small arts organizations stay active and stable. It supports arts projects and teamwork within Maryland communities. The program offers two grant types. The Planning & Development grant supports early research and development. The Implementation grant supports carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants ranging from $1,000 to $4,000. It offers two types of grants: one for planning and development and another for project implementation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis from July 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: The grant is for independent artists, nonprofit arts organizations, local government units, and schools, colleges, or universities in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for two main purposes. The Planning & Development grant supports the early stages of a project, like research and development. The Implementation grant supports carrying out a specific arts project, event, or program.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be based in Maryland to be eligible.
requirements_list: Must be an independent artist, a Maryland-incorporated 501(c)3 nonprofit organization in operation for at least one year, a unit of Maryland local government, or a Maryland college, university, or school.
Organizations applying through a fiscal sponsorship must use a Model A sponsorship.
Applicants must identify a specific event, activity, or project.
Organizations that receive funding through general operating programs from the Maryland State Arts Council are not eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, complete the application in the SmartSimple portal. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed monthly. A panel of experts will review and score all applications. You will receive a notification about the status of your application in the month after the review.

program_name: Data Center Energy Efficiency Grant Program
summary: This competitive program provides incentives to encourage the implementation of cost-effective energy efficiency technologies in Maryland data centers.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_name: FY23 Data Center Energy Efficiency Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers grants for clean energy projects in Maryland data centers. The program helps these facilities install cost-effective, energy-efficient technologies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The total program budget for fiscal year 2023 was $2.4 million. This funding was split between the commercial, industrial, non-profit sector and the agricultural sector.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program serves businesses, manufacturers, data centers, nonprofit organizations, private schools, privately-owned colleges and universities, and agricultural businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support clean energy projects and the installation of cost-effective energy efficiency technologies.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit the program's application form. The agency reviews applications on a first-come, first-served basis until all funds are awarded or the deadline passes.

program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
summary: Data centers that locate or expand in Maryland and create new full-time positions may receive an exemption from Maryland sales and use tax on the purchase of qualified data center personal property.

structured_extraction.program_name: Data Center Maryland Sales and Use Tax Exemption Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers a sales and use tax exemption to data centers that open or grow in Maryland. To qualify, businesses must create new full-time jobs and purchase specific data center property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible businesses receive an exemption from Maryland's sales and use tax on qualifying data center property for 10 years. The benefit period can extend to 20 years if the business invests at least $250 million within the first ten years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that operate data centers and plan to locate or expand in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax exemption applies to the purchase of qualified data center personal property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide but has different investment requirements based on location. Tier 1 areas, which include specific counties and all Opportunity Zones, have a lower investment threshold.
requirements_list: Must be certified as a "Qualified Data Center" by the Maryland Department of Commerce.
Invest at least $2 million in qualified data center personal property if located in a Tier 1 Area.
Invest at least $5 million in qualified data center personal property if located in any other area of the State.
Create at least five new, full-time qualified positions within a three-year period.
Qualified positions must pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage, be filled for at least 12 months, and be new to Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Eligibility Application to the Department of Commerce. Then, Commerce reviews the application and issues a Certificate of Eligibility. Finally, Commerce notifies the Comptroller's Office, which issues the sales and use tax exemption certificate to the business.

summary: Provide below market interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to local governments and other eligible entities to finance drinking water capital improvement projects.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Government

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-interest loans, grants, and loan principal forgiveness. Local governments and other eligible groups can use these funds for projects that improve drinking water systems.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans with interest rates below the market rate, grants, and loan principal forgiveness to finance drinking water capital improvement projects.
