summary: Program provides a State income tax credit to small businesses for hiring qualified veterans. Maryland employers may qualify for a credit equal to 30% of up to the first $6,000 of wages paid to a qualified veteran employee in the first year of employment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a state income tax credit to small businesses that hire qualified veterans. It helps businesses reduce their tax payments based on wages paid to these employees.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Employers could qualify for a tax credit for 30% of the first $6,000 in wages paid to a qualified veteran employee. The maximum credit was $1,800 per veteran. The credit was available for wages paid during the employee's first year of employment between tax years 2017 and 2020.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with 50 or fewer full-time employees are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit offsets a business's state income tax liability. It is based on wages paid to a newly hired, qualified veteran.
requirements_list: Business must have 50 or fewer full-time employees.
Hired employee must be a qualified veteran under program guidelines.
A business may claim the credit for up to 5 qualified veteran employees per year.
The tax credit is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or backward.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To receive the credit, a business submitted application forms, employee self-certification, W-2s or paystubs, and military discharge forms to the Maryland Department of Commerce for certification. After receiving the certificate, the employer filed it with their state tax return using Maryland Tax Form 500CR.

summary: This program provides support for the acquisition, rehabilitation, and restoration of historic properties that offer some form of public benefit and for pre-development costs for some applicants.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Colleges, State University, State Government, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to help with buying, restoring, and fixing historic properties in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants up to $100,000. It typically has about $600,000 available for grants each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY26 grant round is anticipated to open in February, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals who own or manage eligible historic properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds can be used for: buying a historic property; fixing or restoring a historic property. Nonprofits and local governments can also use funds for pre-development costs like studies, surveys, plans, and architectural or engineering services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be for properties in Maryland that are listed in or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.
requirements_list: All applicants except for nonprofit organizations must provide a dollar-for-dollar funding match.
Projects must comply with the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Treatment of Historic Properties.
A preservation easement on the assisted property must be given to the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT).
Work that is already in progress or completed is not eligible for funding.
The applicant must provide written permission from the property owner to undertake the project.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are usually available in February and due in mid-March. The agency makes decisions by July each year. Check the program website starting in September for announcements about the next round. The next round is expected to open in February 2026.

summary: This program provides funding for acquisition, refinancing, rehabilitation, and pre-development costs for historic properties, particularly endangered historic structures for which traditional or commercial loans are not available. In addition, certain nonprofits are eligible to apply for a nonrepayable transfer of funds from the program. This component of the program is new beginning in FY 2024 and is only available to a “qualified cooperating nonprofit organization.”
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Individuals, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_name: Historic Preservation Loan Program for Capital Projects
structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers loans to help preserve historic properties across Maryland. It provides funding for buying, refinancing, rehabilitating, and planning for these properties. Certain nonprofit organizations can also apply for funds that do not need to be paid back.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans with terms up to two years for pre-development projects and up to twenty years for other projects. Interest rates for businesses and individuals are set at 1/8 percent higher than the most recent State general obligation bonds. The loan amount depends on available funds, the borrower's ability to repay, and the property's value, typically not exceeding 80% of the appraised value. The program also offers non-repayable fund transfers, which are like grants, to qualified nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application submission period for the Historic Preservation Loan Program for Capital Projects is now closed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and individuals who own or want to acquire eligible historic properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds can be used for: buying historic properties; refinancing existing loans; repairing and restoring properties; and paying for pre-construction work like studies, plans, and architectural services. Transfer funds for qualified nonprofits can be used to acquire properties for resale, restore properties, or provide loans to other organizations and individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available for historic properties located anywhere in Maryland.
requirements_list: The assisted property must be listed on or eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places.
A preservation easement on the assisted property must be given to the Maryland Historical Trust for loan projects.
Business and individual applicants must demonstrate they could not obtain private financing.
The project must show a public benefit to be competitive.
A fee of $1,000 or 10% of the loan amount, whichever is less, is required.
Homeowner-occupied homes are generally not competitive unless they are exceptionally significant historically.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, contact program staff to discuss your project's eligibility. Next, review the program guidelines and applications. There are different applications for loans and transfers. The process from submitting the application to settlement usually takes six to nine months.

summary: This program provides support for research, survey, planning, and educational activities involving architectural, archeological, or cultural resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives grants for research, surveys, planning, and educational projects. The projects must involve architectural, archaeological, or cultural resources.

structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit organizations and local government jurisdictions. State and federal government entities can also apply as nonprofits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support research, surveys, documentation, planning, and educational activities for historic, architectural, archaeological, or cultural resources. This includes creating historic structure reports, National Register nominations, and preservation plans.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must first submit an Intent to Apply form online by October 15, 2025. Then, they submit the final application online by November 17, 2025. All users must create an account in the grants portal to apply.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and non-profit museum organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support projects that interpret Maryland's history, promote tourism, and provide public education.

summary: To provide leadership and support in promoting the employment, economic self-sufficiency, and independence of individuals with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides services to individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently at home and in their community. It is for people whose main goal is not employment.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers independent living services to help individuals with disabilities be more independent at home and in the community. It also includes the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), which helps individuals 55 or older who are blind or have vision impairment live independently.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program serves individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently. A specific program is also available for blind or vision-impaired individuals who are 55 or older.

The primary goal should be independent living, not employment.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To learn more about independent living services, contact the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC).

summary: A partnership between Maryland DNR, the University of Maryland and the Environmental Protection Agency, to provide research & development funding to University staff,  and  seed capital monies to develop new technologies to accelerate bay restoration.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program is a partnership that provides funding to speed up the restoration of the Chesapeake Bay. It supports the development of new technologies by providing research and development funds to university staff and seed money to Maryland companies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund has two parts. The Research and Development fund provides awards from $30,000 to $100,000. The Seed Capital Fund provides awards from $50,000 to $450,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for students, faculty, and staff from the University of Maryland System, as well as any company based in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds are for the research, development, and commercialization of new technologies that help restore the Chesapeake Bay.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The Research and Development fund is for personnel within the University of Maryland System. The Seed Capital fund is for any company in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants for the Research and Development fund must be students, faculty, or staff from the University of Maryland System.
Applicants for the Seed Capital Fund must be a Maryland company.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program has two parts. To learn more about the Research and Development fund, contact Ronnie Gist at rgist@umd.edu. For information on the Seed Capital Fund, contact Scott Christensen at schris14@umd.edu. For general questions, contact Ari Engelberg.

agency: Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to investigate and prosecute internet crimes against children. The funds help local and state law enforcement agencies and child advocacy centers. This support pays for salaries, training, and equipment.
structured_extraction.agency: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state provides at least $2 million for local law enforcement and the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. Up to 25% of the funds can also support child advocacy centers.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for local and state law enforcement agencies and designated child advocacy centers in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for salaries, training, and equipment. Other eligible costs include contractual services, operating expenses, and travel related to investigating and prosecuting internet crimes against children.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The agency releases a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA), usually in March. Applications are typically due in May. Applicants should review the NOFA document for specific instructions.

program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
summary: This program provides eligible borrowers with low-interest loans to help install cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation improvements for existing or to-be-constructed facilities.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, State Government

structured_extraction.program_name: Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Energy Administration offers low-interest loans to Maryland nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and state agencies. The loans help finance energy efficiency and conservation projects. These projects improve facilities and operations, reduce energy costs, and lower greenhouse gas emissions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans with varying interest rates. Businesses and non-profits can get a 3% rate for micro loans or a 2% rate for traditional loans. Maryland state and local governments receive a 0% interest rate, but they must pay a 1% administrative fee on the loan balance. The total program budget for Fiscal Year 2026 is $4,281,842.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit organizations, local governments, businesses, and state agencies in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to finance energy efficiency and conservation projects. This includes identifying and installing improvements that reduce energy use and costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to eligible organizations located anywhere in the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must use the online application form. There are separate application links for businesses, nonprofits, and local governments, and for state agencies.

summary: Businesses that create a minimum number of new full-time positions may be entitled to state income tax credits of up to $3,000 per job or $5,000 per job in a "revitalization area."

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives businesses an income tax credit for creating new full-time jobs in Maryland. The credit amount is higher for jobs in designated revitalization areas and for hiring qualified military veterans.
list_of_eligible_industries: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Businesses can receive a $3,000 income tax credit for each new full-time job. The credit increases to $5,000 per job if the business is in a revitalization area. If the new hire is a qualified veteran, the credit is $4,000 per job, or $6,000 in a revitalization area. Small businesses hiring a qualified veteran can get a $2,500 credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Credits are certified on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses expanding or creating a new facility in Maryland. Small businesses with 50 or fewer employees that hire qualified military veterans are also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide. The minimum number of new jobs a business must create varies by location: 60 jobs anywhere in the state, 25 jobs in a Priority Funding Area, or 10 jobs in certain counties with lower average employment or income.
requirements_list: Notify the Department of Commerce of intent to seek certification before hiring.
Create the minimum number of net new full-time jobs within a 24-month period.
New positions must be filled for at least 12 months before applying for certification.
Positions must pay at least 150% of the state minimum wage or a prevailing wage rate.
The business must offer employer-provided health insurance, retirement benefits, and paid leave for the new positions.
Small businesses must have 50 or fewer employees to be eligible for the veteran hiring credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the Department of Commerce of its intent to apply before creating the new jobs. The business can submit a preliminary application to check its eligibility. After the new employees have worked for at least 12 months, the business submits a final application to get the tax credit certificate. Small businesses hiring veterans can submit a final application once the veteran has been employed for one year.

program_name: Keep Maryland Beautiful - Bill James Environmental Education Grant
summary: To encourage groups to initiate projects to stimulate understanding of or reduce environmental problems, and to encourage a sense of stewardship for the environment.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to help volunteer groups, nonprofits, communities, and land trusts in Maryland. The funds support projects like environmental education, removing litter, promoting citizen care for the environment, and protecting natural resources.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Environmental Trust, Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Department of Agriculture, and Chesapeake Bay Trust
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants for environmental projects. The specific award amounts are not detailed on the page.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Volunteer groups, nonprofit organizations, communities, schools, municipalities, and local land trusts in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support environmental education projects, litter removal, citizen stewardship activities, protecting natural resources, and tree planting on agricultural land.

The deadline to apply is December 1, 2025. The program announces award winners on March 20. Grantees receive funds by April 15 of the following year and must submit final reports after completing the project.

agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: Provides gap financing to nonprofit organizations to promote affordable housing for households earning less than 50% of area median income. The program is governed by a Board of Trustees and staffed by the Department.
eligibility: County Government, For-Profit, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps make housing more affordable for Maryland households with low incomes. It provides funding for various housing-related costs. These costs include construction, nonprofit developer support, resident services, and operating expenses. A Board of Trustees governs the program, which the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development manages.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding as grants for capacity building, operating costs, and support services. It offers deferred-payment loans or recoverable grants for capital costs. These are repayable if the project is sold or no longer serves low-income residents. Pre-development awards are typically loans that must be repaid.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit organizations, public housing authorities, government agencies, and for-profit companies that develop affordable housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for: capital costs for rental and homeownership housing; financial help for nonprofit developers to build their capacity; supportive services for residents of affordable housing; and operating costs for affordable housing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must serve households earning less than 50% of the area or statewide median income.
Preference is given to projects serving households with incomes below 30% of the median.
Projects should demonstrate readiness and feasibility.
Capital projects must ensure long-term affordability.
Applicants must show a need for the housing in their area.
Projects that use other funding sources are preferred.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period is currently closed. When open, applicants must submit an application along with required legal documents, such as an incumbency certificate and a board resolution.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program

summary: Grants available to nonprofit organizations and state/local government units to foster the creation and expansion of the state’s breweries, distilleries and wineries.

program_name: Maryland Section 5310 Program- Enhanced Mobility for Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Grant
summary:
The Maryland Section 5310 Program, formally known as the Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Program, is funded by the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and administered in Maryland by the Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration (MDOT MTA). The program is designed to improve mobility for older adults and individuals with disabilities by supporting transportation services that go beyond the scope of traditional public transit. Eligible applicants include private nonprofit organizations, state or local government authorities, and public transit agencies that can demonstrate their services address the needs of seniors and individuals with disabilities. To qualify, applicants must be able to show coordination with other transportation and human service providers, demonstrate financial and managerial capacity to manage federal funds, and commit to maintaining vehicles or equipment purchased through the program in compliance with FTA guidelines. The program also requires applicants to meet federal cost share requirements: capital projects are funded at 80 percent federal and 20 percent local match, while operating projects are funded at 50 percent federal and 50 percent local match.

In Maryland, the 5310 Program plays a critical role in ensuring that seniors and individuals with disabilities can maintain independence, access essential services, and participate fully in community life. MDOT MTA administers the competitive application process, prioritizing projects that demonstrate strong coordination, meet an identified transportation gap, and show the ability to sustain services over time. Funding may be used for traditional capital projects, such as accessible vehicles, technology, and mobility management programs, as well as nontraditional services that expand or enhance transportation options. By providing these targeted resources, the program helps close gaps in mobility, enhances quality of life for vulnerable populations, and supports a more inclusive and accessible transportation network across the state.

program_name: Safe Streets and Roads for All
summary: The U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program provides grants to local, regional, and Tribal communities for implementation, planning, and demonstration activities as part of a systematic approach to prevent deaths and serious injuries on the nation’s roadways. The primary purpose of implementation grants is to construct projects or fund operational strategies identified in an approved Safety Action Plan and/ or complete project feasibility, design, and development required to implement identified projects. Implementation grants may also fund supplemental planning and demonstration activities as a component of the grant. Planning grants may fund the development of a Safety Action Plan, supplemental planning activities to include plan updates, topical sub-plans, additional road safety audits, or follow-up efforts needed to update an Action Plan, and demonstration activities that inform the development of a Safety Action Plan through data collection. Examples of eligible demonstration activities include: feasibility studies using quick-build strategies that inform permanent projects in the future (paint, plastic posts, delineators, removable barriers, reallocation of roadway space), MUTCD engineering studies that further safety applications (evaluating need for high-visibility crosswalks, markings, or bike lane treatments), pilot programs for behavior or operational activities that must include at least one element of the Safe System Approach and, pilot projects that utilize innovative technologies that have not yet been adopted in the community (speed cameras, variable speed limits, adaptive signal timing, adaptive lighting).
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, Regional, State Government

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers two types of grants. Implementation grants help build projects and use strategies from an approved Safety Action Plan. These can also fund project design and development. Planning grants help create or update a Safety Action Plan. They can also fund safety audits and demonstration activities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local, regional, and Tribal communities, including county governments, towns, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support planning, demonstration, and implementation activities to improve road safety. Planning grants help develop or update Safety Action Plans. Implementation grants fund construction projects or safety strategies identified in an action plan. Demonstration activities can include feasibility studies using quick-build strategies, pilot programs for safety behaviors, and testing new technologies like speed cameras or adaptive signals.
requirements_list: Implementation grants require an approved Safety Action Plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a refundable tax credit to theatrical production companies. The credit equals 25% of the production costs spent in Maryland. The credit is refundable, meaning the company can receive a payment even if it owes no state income tax.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a refundable tax credit of 25% for qualified production costs spent in Maryland. The maximum credit is $2 million for a single production.

It also covers salaries for work in Maryland, advertising, facility and equipment rentals, vehicle leases, food, lodging, and travel to Maryland for employees.
requirements_list: Estimated total direct production costs in Maryland must exceed $100,000.
The production must be a for-profit National Touring or Pre-Broadway live stage theatrical production.
National Touring Productions must have at least two public performances in Maryland and then perform for four or more weeks in at least four cities outside the state.
Pre-Broadway Productions must have at least eight public performances in Maryland and be prepared for a Broadway presentation within twelve months of its final Maryland performance.
The applicant must demonstrate it has financing for the project.
Productions with total direct costs over $250,000 must provide an independent, third-party auditor's report.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit an Application for Qualification by email before starting any work in Maryland. The Department will review it and send a Letter of Qualification within 30 days if approved. Second, submit an Application Addendum before the first rehearsal. Third, after the production finishes, apply for the final Tax Credit Certificate within 180 days. You must include final documents and an auditor's report if your costs were over $250,000. Finally, file your state income tax return with the certificate to claim the credit.

agency: Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing, & Regulation
summary: Provide temporary financial assistance to Maryland workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own. Establish rates and collect taxes from Maryland employers to finance benefits.  Conduct appeals for claimants/employers when disputes arise.
application_due: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
assistance_nonfinancial: Regulatory Program, Services, Technical Assistance/Information, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program offers temporary financial help to people who have lost their jobs for reasons that are not their fault. Qualified individuals may receive benefits for up to 26 weeks.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides temporary financial assistance for up to 26 weeks. The specific benefit amount depends on your past earnings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applicant must file as soon as possible upon separation from employment
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are unemployed through no fault of their own.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds provide financial assistance for living expenses during unemployment.
requirements_list: Must be unemployed through no fault of your own.
Must register for the Maryland Workforce Exchange.
Must document weekly job search activities.
Must complete a weekly certification to continue receiving benefits.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, find out if you qualify. Second, gather your personal information and employment history for the last 18 months. Third, file a claim online in the Maryland Unemployment Insurance Portal (BEACON) or by phone. Fourth, document your weekly job search activities in the Maryland Workforce Exchange. Fifth, complete a weekly certification to continue your benefits.

program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
summary: The UPLIFT program finances strategically targeted affordable single family, for-sale development to elevate property values in historically red-lined neighborhoods with the aim of building household wealth. It couples its development loans to build new housing with a commitment from DHCD to offer grants and loans to nearby “Legacy Homeowners,” often living in energy inefficient and deteriorated housing.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps build affordable homes in historically underserved areas. It provides funding to cover the 'appraisal gap,' which is the difference between the cost to build a home and its market sale price. The program aims to increase property values, create homeownership opportunities, and build wealth for families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding to cover the 'appraisal gap.' This gap is the difference between the total cost to build or renovate a property and its final market sale price.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for nonprofit and for-profit housing developers, builders, and community organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds help with costs to acquire, develop, build, and sell affordable homes. The funding specifically covers the appraisal gap, which is the difference between the project cost and the final sale price.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in qualified areas, which include low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. An official map on the program website shows the specific eligible locations.
requirements_list: Applicants must schedule and attend a pre-application meeting before applying.
A $1,000 non-refundable application fee is required per project.
Applicants must submit both an electronic and a physical hard copy of the application.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, you must review the program guide and schedule a pre-application meeting. After the meeting, you request access to the online application portal. Next, complete the application package, which includes project details and financials. Then, you pay the $1,000 application fee. You must submit the application both electronically via Dropbox and as a hard copy to the agency's office. The agency then reviews and scores the application. If your project is approved, you will receive a commitment letter.

summary: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is pleased to offer grants to support tree planting efforts in communities that have been impacted by transportation projects through the MDOT Urban Tree Grant Program. These grants are offered in partnership with the Maryland Urban and Community Forest Committee (MUCFC). To learn more about MUCFC visit their website at https://www.marylandforestryfoundation.org/programs/community-grant-opportunities/mucfc/
eligibility: County Government, Municipalities/Towns, Non-Profit, State Colleges, State University, Other

structured_extraction.program_name: MDOT Urban Tree Program Grant Application
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Transportation offers grants for tree planting projects. The program supports communities affected by transportation projects. It works in partnership with the Maryland Urban and Community Forest Committee.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants of up to $5,000 for eligible tree planting projects. Additional funds are available for Pocket Forest plantings.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: This application is closed. Please contact the administrator if you have questions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for non-profits, schools, community groups, higher education institutions, and local governments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for tree and Pocket Forest planting projects. This includes project maintenance costs like watering, weeding, and mulching. Up to 5% of the grant can also pay for volunteer outreach, signs, or project promotion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in communities where a state transportation project removed trees. The state gives priority to projects in areas affected by environmental justice issues or the heat island effect.
requirements_list: Must get approval from the county Forestry Board before the application deadline.
Planted tree species must be native to the area.
Projects with matching funds or in-kind support receive preference.
Funding cannot be used for required mitigation planting.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, get your project approved by your county Forestry Board. Then, submit an application through the Maryland OneStop system before the deadline. Your application must include a site plan, a photo of the site, a list of proposed native plants, any required permit information, and a maintenance plan.

summary: Provides financial assistance for equipment maintenance or purchase and training to rural fire companies to improve their ability to fight wildfires.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives money and technical help to rural volunteer fire departments. The funds help them buy or maintain equipment and get training to better fight wildfires.
structured_extraction.agency: MARYLAND DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES FOREST SERVICE
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants up to $3,500 per department. It requires a 50/50 cost-share match from the fire department.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rural volunteer fire departments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can pay for wildland firefighting equipment. This includes protective clothing, power tools like chainsaws, hoses, nozzles, and communication radios. Money can also cover off-road vehicles (ATVs/UTVs) and wildland firefighting training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is for fire departments that serve a rural area or a community with 10,000 or fewer people, based on the latest census data.
requirements_list: Must provide a 50/50 cost share match.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit the web application before the deadline. You will receive a confirmation email. 2. The department will notify you if your application was approved or denied by October 15, 2025. 3. If approved, you will receive more documents to submit after you make purchases. 4. Make all purchases before December 31, 2025 and submit paperwork by January 15, 2026. 5. The Maryland Forest Service will reimburse your department within 45 days of receiving the final documents.

summary: Serves as a source of financing for small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Maryland’s Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The program helps businesses create or retain jobs and operates by participating with banks and other lenders, if applicable.
application_due: Revolving Loan Fund loan applications accepted on a continual basis.
contact_name: Ms. Chris Funk, Business Development Loan Officer, Tri County Council for Western Maryland
assistance_financial: Direct Loan, Direct Payment/Specified Use, Loan, Other

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides loans to small businesses in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The goal is to help businesses locate or expand in the area and to create or save jobs. The fund uses repaid loans to provide new loans to other businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans from $10,000 to $500,000. Loan terms can be up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like buildings or equipment. The interest rate is the prime rate plus one percent, with a minimum rate of five percent.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program is for small businesses, including for-profit corporations, non-profit organizations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for business acquisition, buying commercial real estate, building improvements, equipment purchases, leasehold improvements, start-up costs, and working capital.
requirements_list: The project must create or retain at least one job for every $30,000 borrowed.
An application fee of $250 is required ($25 for loans between $10,000-$25,000).
A 1.5% loan origination fee is charged at closing (waived for loans between $10,000-$25,000).
Collateral is required and may include real estate, equipment liens, personal guarantees, and key person life insurance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, you need to submit an inquiry form. There is a non-refundable application fee for loan processing. The program uses standard underwriting practices to review applications.

program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program
summary: Maryland's Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program provides financial assistance to individuals and corporations to establish a new winery or vineyard in the State or complete capital improvements at an existing winery or vineyard. Commerce will provide a grant to an individual or corporation for 25% of “qualified capital expenses.”

structured_extraction.program_name: Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program (WVEDG)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives financial help to individuals and companies. They can use the funds to start a new winery or vineyard in Maryland. They can also use the money for major upgrades to an existing one.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a grant for 25% of qualified capital costs. Qualified costs are expenses for buying and installing equipment or agricultural materials.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for individuals or companies that operate or want to establish a winery or vineyard in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used for qualified capital expenses. This includes buying and installing equipment or agricultural materials for producing wine or growing grapes. Examples include barrels, bottling equipment, tractors, and fruit plants. The grant does not cover the cost of constructing buildings, utilities, labor, or general supplies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The winery or vineyard must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: A qualified winery must hold a Class 3 or Class 4 winery license from the Comptroller of Maryland.
A qualified vineyard must be at least one continuous acre of agricultural land in Maryland used only for growing grapes for a licensed Maryland winery.
Applicants must submit a detailed report of expenses with proof of purchase.
Capital expenses must be for either establishing a new winery or vineyard, or making capital improvements to an existing one.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit an online application to the Maryland Department of Commerce by the deadline. The application must include a detailed report of expenses with supporting documents. Commerce will review the application and certify the grant amount.

program_name: Woodland Improvement Program (WIP) and Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
summary: Provide cost share monies for implementation of reforestation and timber stand improvement practices including technical assistance in planning these practices.

structured_extraction.program_name: Woodland Improvement Program (WIP) and Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
structured_extraction.program_description: These programs offer financial and technical help to landowners, farmers, and forest managers. They provide cost-sharing payments to help install or use conservation practices on agricultural and forest land. The goal is to support reforestation, timber stand improvement, and other environmental practices.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources; USDA Natural Resource Conservation Service
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Woodland Improvement Program (WIP) pays up to 65% of the costs for eligible practices. The Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP) typically funds practices at 50%. However, new farmers or those with limited resources may receive cost-shares up to 90%. Both programs also provide technical assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Landowners, agricultural producers, and people or businesses managing forestry projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support various conservation and forestry management activities. For the Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP), this includes nutrient and manure management, pest management, and wildlife habitat enhancement. For the Woodland Incentive Program (WIP), uses include tree planting, thinning, pruning, prescribed burning, site preparation for reforestation, and herbicide treatments.
requirements_list: For the Woodland Improvement Program, you must own at least 5 but no more than 1,000 forest acres.
For the Woodland Improvement Program, you cannot have received program assistance for the same practice in the last 15 years.
For the Environmental Quality Incentives Program, the land must be cropland, rangeland, grassland, pasture, or private non-industrial forestland.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, contact your local department forester. For the Woodland Improvement Program, you will apply for specific practices. If your application is approved, you complete the work and pay for it. A forester then inspects the work. After approval, you submit your invoices and proof of payment to the forester to be processed for reimbursement.
